text:
SupportBot: New escalation from Support queue → SUP-3112: "Invoice tokens higher than Console by ~6%" (Hosted API). Customer asking for breakdown + why mismatch.

Dev Patel: Hey folks, can someone help with a crisp explanation we can send to the customer + the right links? They’re comparing Console Usage (month view) to the invoice line item and seeing ~6% higher on invoice.

Rachel Kim: +1, customer is pretty upset. They want something concrete (not "pipeline differences"). If we have a known edge case, we should call it out.

Emily Stone: Do we know if they’re looking at the right time zone / invoice window? We’ve had a few where Console is local time and invoice is UTC month boundary.

Dev Patel: They’re saying "Jan 1–Jan 31" in console, invoice is January usage. Not sure on TZ. They also mentioned a bunch of streaming requests (they cancel responses sometimes).

Logan Wright: A few likely causes, ordered by probability:
1) Console usage page is showing “request timestamp” bucketed in viewer TZ (or account TZ), invoice is always UTC and based on usage_event_time (server-side). Boundary effects can be a few % if they run big jobs around midnight.
2) Streaming disconnect accounting: if client disconnects mid-stream, we bill tokens generated up to disconnect. Console historically undercounted partial streams in some views. (There was an issue; not sure if fixed in prod for Jan.)
3) Retries: invoice counts *billed* tokens; console might include/exclude retry attempts depending on the toggle.

Nadia Rahman: Re (2) — we had a bug for a subset of streaming events where the console aggregator dropped partial completions when `client_disconnect=true` but `usage.finalized=false` at the time of snapshot. Billing pipeline reconciles after finalize, so invoice is higher. Fix is in flight but Jan data may be impacted.

Chloe Martin: Console side: current usage page shows the "invoice-style" aggregate for most tenants, but if they’re on the older usage breakdown (some accounts still are), it can lag and/or miss partial streaming. If you send me org slug/account id I can confirm which view they’re on.

Dev Patel: Account is "LumenDesk" (org_id: org_7Q2...). Region mostly us-east. Models: a lot of `llama-70b-chat` and some embeddings.

Allison Grant: If this is the same pattern as the other case last week, there was also an anomaly where backfill jobs temporarily made console totals look lower until the next daily rollup. But the customer sees invoice vs console right now, so they need a "what is billed" explanation.

Emily Stone: We should give them:
- what’s billed (input + output tokens actually processed)
- what’s not billed (tokens after disconnect aren’t billed; failed requests may not be billed depending on outcome)
- why console may differ (time zone, in-flight finalization, old view)
- offer: we can provide a CSV breakdown (by day/model) to reconcile.

Logan Wright: + links:
- Meter defs (Hosted API) w/ streaming + retries notes: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/FIN/Hosted+API+Meter+Definitions+v3
- Invoice line mapping and mismatch causes: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/FIN/Invoice+Line+Item+Mapping+to+Telemetry
- Internal runbook (for us) if they want evidence package: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/FIN/Billing+Discrepancy+Triage+Runbook

Nadia Rahman: For the customer-facing explanation, I’d word streaming like:
"For streaming responses, we meter tokens as they are generated on the server. If the client disconnects mid-response, we bill only tokens generated before the disconnect. Those partial streams can take up to 24h to finalize in usage reporting, so the Console month view can temporarily appear lower than the invoice-ready totals." (assuming their invoice is generated from finalized totals).

Chloe Martin: I checked org_7Q2 — they’re still on the legacy usage page (behind feature flag `console_usage_v2=false`). That view is known to undercount partial streaming and is in local TZ.

Dev Patel: That explains the discrepancy. What’s the clean ask/offer here? Upgrade them to new console view?

Chloe Martin: Yes. We can flip them to usage v2; it should match invoice aggregation rules (UTC window + same rounding). I can do it today, but it won’t retroactively change historical in all charts until nightly rollup.

Emily Stone: From Finance side, we should avoid promising "exact match" if there are still accepted tolerances, but we can say "should align" and we can provide line-level breakdown if needed.

Rachel Kim: Can someone give me a 4–6 sentence response I can paste into the ticket? Also customer asked for "links to usage breakdown".

Logan Wright: Draft you can send (edit as needed):
"Thanks for flagging this — invoices are generated from Redwood’s server-side metering of tokens processed (input + output) in UTC for the invoice period. The Console month view can differ when (a) the usage view is bucketed in a different time zone, and/or (b) streaming requests that are interrupted finalize after the initial rollup, which can temporarily undercount partial streaming usage in the Console. We can enable the updated Console usage breakdown for your org, which uses the same aggregation window and rules as invoicing. If you’d like, we can also share a per-day/per-model CSV export for January to reconcile the totals on your side." 

Nadia Rahman: + add one line: "Note: we do not bill tokens generated after a client disconnect; only tokens generated before disconnect are metered." That addresses the overbilling concern.

Allison Grant: If they ask "why 6%", we can say: "Most of the delta comes from partial streaming sessions that were finalized after the Console snapshot" (true given legacy view). But don’t mention "bug" unless we’re sure.

Emily Stone: Agree. Say "known reporting lag for partial streams" / "legacy view behavior".

Dev Patel: Cool. Rachel, I’ll drop you the response + links. Also looping in Chloe to flip feature flag.

Rachel Kim: Perfect. Please do flip ASAP; customer is checking in tomorrow.

Chloe Martin: On it. Will enable `console_usage_v2` for org_7Q2 now. :thumbsup:

Chloe Martin: (later) Feature flag enabled for org_7Q2. New Usage page should appear after refresh; full backfilled month chart should align after nightly rollup.

Dev Patel: Thanks all. I’ll update SUP-3112 with the explanation + offer CSV export if they want deeper reconciliation.

Emily Stone: If they still dispute after v2 view, tag me and we’ll pull the invoice_run export + do a targeted reconcile sample.

Rachel Kim: Added to ticket with links + noted we enabled updated usage view. Will report back if they push for a credit.
